display.title: Rosh Hashanah: Crowning Hashem as King of the World
display.summary_short: Why do we keep saying 'Hashem Melech' on Rosh Hashanah? Uncle Yossi tells how Adam first crowned Hashem as King, and how we crown Him again each year with prayer and the shofar.
display.summary_long: A Rosh Hashanah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi asks why we need to call Hashem King when He is the Creator and Master of the world anyway. He turns the clock back 5,749 years to the very first Rosh Hashanah, the sixth day of creation, when Adam HaRishon opened his eyes and was the first to proclaim 'Hashem Melech', which gave Hashem great delight. To remember this, the Levi'im in the Beis HaMikdash sang 'Hashem Malach' every Friday, and the machzor repeats 'Hashem Melech, Hashem Malach, Hashem Yimloch l'olam va'ed' again and again. Like a king crowned with the sound of trumpets, Hashem accepts our coronation when we blow the shofar, and agrees to be our King for the coming year, which the Rebbe said would be a year of miracles. The 'order of the day' for both days of Rosh Hashanah is to say these words as often as possible.
display.lesson: On Rosh Hashanah we make Hashem happy by crowning Him as our King, and He blesses us with a good and sweet year.
